summary: Iteration 16 tests THREE new deliverables: (1) 4 replaced step images + 7 rebuilt videos serve correctly, (2) Badge Shelf share buttons per earned badge work with clipboard fallback + toast, (3) new Safety Assessment /email-mediator endpoint + dialog. Plus the coercive-threshold scoring change (single yes -> Level 2). 28/28 backend pytest tests pass. Frontend flows verified end-to-end: badge share -> clipboard toast, IPV assessment Level-4 submit -> results -> mediator dialog opens, empty-input disables send, typed email enables send, send triggers 502 error path (Resend domain unverified in preview) which is acceptable per acceptance criteria. Cancel + Close(X) buttons both dismiss the dialog.

integration_issues.flow: Safety Assessment: Send to mediator error toast content
integration_issues.issue: When Resend backend fails (502 EmailSendError -> unverified sacoparentsapp.online domain), Cloudflare's default error page HTML replaces the FastAPI JSON body. The toast then surfaces Cloudflare's raw text ('The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare...') instead of the intended friendly fallback ('Couldn't send to your mediator right now.'). Non-blocking: the dialog closes, the send button re-enables, and the acceptance criteria treat any error-toast as a pass. To fix long-term: catch Resend errors in the backend and return 503 (which the frontend already maps to a friendly copy path) instead of 502 — or add a Cloudflare 502 detection in the frontend catch block and swap in the fallback string.

action_items: OPTIONAL/UX: When Resend Domain-Not-Verified triggers backend 502, the current Cloudflare 502 HTML page bleeds into the toast content. Consider mapping Resend send errors to 503 in email_service.EmailSendError -> HTTPException at the /email-mediator endpoint so users see the friendly 'Email isn't configured on this environment' copy (or add a Cloudflare-error detection in the frontend catch).
critical_code_review_comments: safety_assessment_routes.py score_assessment(): new rule 'len(coercive_hits) >= 1 or section_1_yes >= 4 -> Level 2' correctly implemented. HTTP endpoint returns matching result. No regressions to Levels 1/3/4.
safety_assessment_routes.py::email_assessment_to_mediator: validation order is safe (email format -> demo.local -> is_guest -> parent_email demo.local). All four gates fire correctly.
BadgeShelf.jsx::shareBadge properly detects navigator.share vs clipboard fallback and surfaces distinct toasts. Aborted share (user cancels sheet) is treated as noop — good UX.
SafetyAssessment.jsx::MediatorEmailDialog properly gates send-button disabled state on empty input AND on `sending` flag — no double-submit possible.

MINOR UX: the axios error handler in sendToMediator relies on err.response.data.detail being JSON. When an upstream gateway (Cloudflare) rewrites 5xx bodies to HTML, the toast surfaces the raw HTML text. Consider stringifying or type-checking err.response.data before using it.
